title: Venezuela : Country Finance Manager – Caracas
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
**Fixed term | 6 months | ASAP**

## Acted

***Who we are***

Acted works with 19 million people across 43 countries at the intersection of humanitarian, development, climate and environmental programming. We draw on deep contextual knowledge and embrace emerging technologies to save lives, alleviate suffering, and protect and restore our planet. Working in collaboration with a growing ecosystem of local, national and international partners, we pursue one shared objective: a 3Zero World – Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon and Zero Poverty.

***Who we are looking for***

You bring the core competencies required for classical humanitarian and development work, alongside an active climate and environmental conscience, and you can navigate the challenges that arise when human and environmental suffering intersect. You have an entrepreneurial mindset: you see opportunities, connect dots, adapt your approach to different environments, and take measured risks in pursuit of results. You balance principles with pragmatism, and ambition with humility.

## Acted Colombia - Venezuela

Colombia continues being affected by a complex humanitarian crisis, characterized by multidimensional factors such as protracted armed conflict, natural disasters, and mixed movement/displacement dynamics (both internal and external displacement). Moreover, the crisis is exacerbated by the limited presence of state actors in several zones of the country, especially in hard-to-reach and rural areas combined with high poverty rates (36.6%) and food insecurity levels (30%) resulting in approximately 9.1 million people estimated in need of humanitarian assistance.

In parallel, Venezuela continues facing a severe humanitarian crisis, with nearly 8 million people having migrated since 2014, marking the largest exodus in Latin America. 7.9 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance due to the deterioration of basic public services and a deep economic crisis characterized by high inflation rates and lack of purchase power, resulting in an estimated 56% of its population living in extreme poverty. Moreover, according to the OECD, Venezuela also ranks among the top 3 countries with the highest increase in human fragility, while 40% of the population experience moderate to severe food insecurity and 62% face restriction on access to drinking water. Highly vulnerable communities, living in rural and border areas are affected the most, and 1.4 million children are estimated in need of protections assistance.

## You will be in charge of

The Country Finance Manager (CFM) is a key member of the Management Team at country level. He/she will be responsible for Acted financial management in-country under the authority of the Country Director and Finance & Administrative Director in HQ. The CFM ensures that national legislation is adhered to, and that Acted’s financial standards are applied in terms of accounting, financial control systems, internal / external reporting processes, in order to ensure an efficient use of resources. He/She leads, provides technical support and capacity building to the country finance and administrative staff. The CFM shall alert the Country Director and Finance Director in case some major problems arise with a potential financial impact on the mission.

***Main duties***

1\. Accounting and treasury Management

- *Accounting management – supervise the accounting cycle for the mission*
- *Treasury management – ensure a controlled and smooth cash management*

2\. Commitment of expenditures, budget control, & Financial Management

- *Commitment of expenditure – guaranty budget availability and compliance to Acted and donor’s procedures before releasing payments*
- *Project budget follow-up, mission’s cost control, internal & external audits – anticipate and mitigate financial risks ensuring operations are run in a compliant and cost-efficient manner*

3\. Project financial cycle management

- *Develop project budgets and reports – ensure the financial feasibility of projects, respecting Acted and donors’ rules and deadlines*

4\. Team leadership & other tasks

## Expected skills and qualifications

- Msc in Finance, Audit, Business Management, Economics or equivalent;
- 3+ years of solid experience in financial & budget management;
- Excellent financial and analytical skills;
- Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting on programme financial performance;
- Ability to manage a financial team and demonstrate leadership;
- Ability to monitor and evaluate financial skills of teams through capacity-building efforts;
- Ability to undertake serious responsibilities and to manage stress efficiently;
- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility;
- Prior knowledge of the region an asset.

## Conditions

- Salary between 3300 and 3500€ monthly (before income tax), depending on the level of education, security level, etc as well as a monthly living allowance of $300
- Accommodation and food provided in Acted guesthouse
- Pension, health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance (& unemployment insurance for EU citizens)
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: up to 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract
- R&R every 3 months, flight tickets covered up to $500 and allowance of $200
- Annual leave of 25 to 43 days per year
- One week pre-departure training in Acted HQ, including a 4-days in situ security training
- Tax advice (free 30-minute call with a tax consultant)
- Psychological assistance
- This position is classified as an **international staff position** under Acted’s recruitment framework. Eligibility for an international contract is therefore required.

title: Global Communication Coordinator
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified and enthusiastic Global Communication Coordinator.

**About the job**

You will be working with a diverse and dynamic team at the Mixed Migration Centre (MMC), which is an intrinsic part of DRC. MMC is a leading source for independent and high-quality data, research, analysis and expertise on mixed migration. MMC aims to increase understanding of mixed migration, to positively impact global and regional migration policies, to inform evidence-based protection responses for people on the move and to stimulate forward thinking in public and policy debates on mixed migration. MMC’s overarching focus is on human rights and protection for all people on the move.  
Reporting to the director of MMC, the Global Communication Coordinator leads and oversees the implementation of all MMC activities in relation to internal and external communication and visibility, finalization of MMC publications for release, report launches, organization of events and MMC’s online (social media, website, etc.) presence

  
Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

***Communications strategy***

- Lead the implementation of MMC's external communication strategy across the global team and regional hubs.

***Publications, events, online presence and campaigns***

- Oversee the updating and maintenance of the MMC website.
- Be responsible for all MMC social media output, including the MMC X, LinkedIn and YouTube accounts and channels.
- Oversee the finalisation of all MMC research outputs in line with MMC editorial and brand guidelines, and act as guardian of MMC's global publication calendar.
- Lead the release of all publications, including the Quarterly Mixed Migration Updates, and develop and execute the associated communication plans and toolkits, including social media launches.
- Oversee the release of MMC's regional and global newsletters.
- Lead the implementation of the extensive communication campaign around the annual Mixed Migration Review (MMR).
- Prepare and deliver virtual and in-person events (registrations, social media promotion, hosting of online conference platforms, etc.).

***External engagement and identification of opportunities***

- Work closely with MMC regional hub staff to proactively identify and develop new communication tools, such as podcasts, videos on key research findings and human-interest stories.
- Track events calendars, and signal and organise speaking opportunities for MMC.
- Draft press releases, maintain an up-to-date list of MMC media contacts and strengthen media outreach.
- Engage with global and regional partners to disseminate MMC research products.
- Liaise with DRC Communication and Press offices at HQ (Copenhagen), Geneva, Brussels and in the regions.

***Coordination, reporting and management***

- Report on MMC's external visibility (e.g. monthly and annual website and social media statistics, event attendance and post-event surveys, external references to MMC) as input into MMC's Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning.
- Manage the work of MMC's communication officers/specialists (currently two).

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to be able to take the lead on your tasks and be able to oversee all internal and external communication and visibility activities across the global MMC network. Attention to detail while capable of keeping the big picture in sight is key in this role. Moreover, we also expect the following:

*Required*

- 5+ years of professional experience in external communication, ideally in the NGO, UN, research or humanitarian/development sector.
- Proven experience planning and running social media campaigns and managing social media output.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with an excellent eye for detail.
- Strong organisational and multitasking skills, and flexibility to manage many tasks of varying size at the same time.
- Full proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint); proficiency in WordPress, InDesign and Canva.
- Ability to develop data visualisations using different visualisation software.
- Ability to work effectively with a team based remotely across several countries.
- University degree within relevant field of study

*Desirable*

- Strong affinity with matters relating to (mixed) migration, forced displacement and humanitarian/development work.
- Previous work with NGOs or UN in the development or humanitarian sector
- Fluency in French and/or Spanish
- Academic background in migration studies, including some experience in research (field-level research is a strong asset)

All employees are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Work location: Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken station

Start date: 1st December 2026

End date: 31 June 2027

The position is temporary as it is currently funded until the end of June, but likely to be extended, upon donor funding confirmation.

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and AC The position is at “fuldmægtig” level. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply.

Please note that you need to have the right to work in Denmark (through nationality or existing work visa) in order to be considered for this role.

**Further information**

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Gretel Ana Martin Araya by email gretel.araya@mixedmigration.org. We will do our best to respond to as many inquiries as possible.

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website [drc.ngo](https://reliefweb.int/javascript:void(0)).

*Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.*

title: Supply Chain Intern
body:
**Titre du poste: Supply Chain Intern**

**Supervisé par: Supply Chain Manager**

**Répondant à: Supply Chain Manager**

**Supervise: NA**

**Lieu d’affectation: Yaoundé avec possibilité d’appui dans les autres bases DRC**

**Zone intervention: Cameroun**

**Période considérée: 06 à 12 mois**

**Type de contrat (National): Contrat de stage (uniquement réservé aux ressortissants Camerounais)**

**Salaire et avantages: Allocation mensuelle**

**Introduction**

Le Conseil Danois pour les Réfugiés (DRC) porte assistance aux réfugiés et aux personnes déplacées à travers le monde : nous fournissons une aide d’urgence à ces personnes, nous combattons pour leurs droits et nous renforçons leurs opportunités pour un meilleur futur. Nous travaillons dans des zones affectées par les conflits, ainsi que le long des routes de déplacements, et au sein des pays dans lesquels les réfugiés s’établissent. En coopération avec les communautés locales, nous nous efforçons d’atteindre des solutions responsables et durables. Nous travaillons pour une intégration réussie des communautés vulnérables et, lorsque cela est possible, à la réalisation de leur souhait de retour chez eux.

Le Conseil Danois pour les Réfugiés (DRC en sigle, pour Danish Refugee Council) a été fondé au Danemark en 1956 et est depuis devenu une organisation humanitaire internationale avec plus de 7,000 employés et de 8,000 volontaires. Ayant son siège établi à Copenhague, et présent dans 40 pays, le DRC est une organisation d’aide non gouvernementale, à but non-lucratif, politiquement neutre et indépendante et non-confessionnelle.

Notre vision est une vie avec dignité pour toutes les personnes déplacées dans le monde. Tous nos efforts reposent sur notre boussole morale : l’humanité, le respect, l’indépendance, la neutralité, la participation, l’honnêteté et la transparence.

**1. Contexte**

Sous la direction du bureau régional de Dakar et en lien étroit avec les interventions menées dans la République centrafricaine (RCA) voisine, DRC a commencé ses opérations au Cameroun en 2018 afin de répondre aux besoins humanitaires des réfugiés de RCA et des populations camerounaises vulnérables dans la région de l’Adamaoua.

DRC a initialement établi ses opérations à Meiganga, dans la région de l’Est puis à Djohong et à Garoua-BoulaÏ. En 2024, DRC a étendu ses interventions au département du Mayo-Tsanaga, dans la région de l’Extrême-Nord, en coordination avec les autres acteurs humanitaires, afin de mettre en œuvre une réponse en matière de moyens de subsistance au profit des réfugiés les plus vulnérables du camp de Minawao.

En 2025, DRC a également étendu ses opérations à la région du Nord-Ouest, avec l’ouverture d’un bureau à Bamenda.

**2. Objet**

Sous l’encadrement technique du Supply Chain Manager basé à Yaounde, le/la Supply Chain Intern aura pour mission d’apporter un appui à la gestion des affaires courantes du département Supply Chain à Yaoundé.

le/la Supply Chain Intern peut également se rendre dans d’autres bases afin d’apporter un appui logistique, selon les besoins et à la discrétion du Supply Chain Manager.

**3. Fonctions**

Sous les directives du Supply Chain Manager, le/la Supply Chain Intern est chargé de :

- Exécuter les fonctions logistiques déléguées conformément au plan d’action ;
- Mener les activités logistiques opérationnelles quotidiennes et assure leur suivi ;
- Contribuer à l’administration des ressources afin que les livrables soient réalisés suivant les budgets, les délais et les normes établis ;
- Préparer les rapports logistiques suivant les demandes du bureau pays ;
- Veiller au bon archivage de tous les documents justificatifs ;
- Promouvoir et partager des idées pour améliorer la fonction logistique ;
- Assurer le bon fonctionnement de la flotte
- Assurer le bon suivi de la maison d'hôtes pour le personnel
- Effectuer d’autres tâches attribuées par le supérieur hiérarchique.

Le/la Supply Chain Intern a pour mission d’assurer la mise en œuvre au quotidien des tâches qui comprend :

- **Appui à la gestion des stocks (5% de son temps) ;**
- **Appui à la gestion des achats (10% de son temps) ;**
- **Appui à la gestion de la flotte (35% de son temps) ;**
- **Appui à la Gestion des immobilisations ( 25% de son temps);**
- **Appui à la gestion des archives (25% de son temps) ;**

**4. Qualifications requises**

**Expériences et compétences techniques** :

- Niveau académique équivalent à un Bac+2 minimum, universitaire dans le domaine de la logistique, de la comptabilité/économie, ou formation de type Bioforce ;
- Une connaissance des logiciels de gestion logistique (SIGL, Dynamics, …) est préférable ;
- Excellente maîtrise de Microsoft Office ;
- Excellente maitrise des outils Excel ;
- Excellentes compétences en termes d’analyse et de rapportage ;
- Excellente compétences interpersonnelles et habilité démontrée à travailler sous pression et dans des conditions stressantes ;
- Bonne compréhension du contexte de travail au sein d’un environnement international.
- Être bilingue (Français et anglais) est un avantage.

**5. Compétences et qualités exigées**

- À ce poste, vous devez démontrer les cinq compétences essentielles du DRC, à savoir :
    - **Viser l'excellence :** vous vous concentrez sur l'obtention de résultats tout en garantissant un processus efficace. Vous vous efforcez de produire un travail précis, approfondi et professionnel avec une utilisation optimale du temps et des efforts.
    - **Collaborer** : vous coopérez avec et impliquez les parties concernées, recherchant activement leur opinion et partageant des informations clés avec elles. Vous soutenez et faites confiance aux autres, tout en encourageant les commentaires.
    - **Prendre les rênes** : Vous prenez la responsabilité et donnez la priorité à votre travail en fonction de la vision et des objectifs généraux de DRC. Vous prenez l’initiative face à un défi ou une opportunité et vous recherchez des solutions innovantes.
    - **Communiquer** : vous écrivez et parlez efficacement et honnêtement tout en adaptant votre style et votre ton à la situation. Vous écoutez activement les autres et les impliquez dans le dialogue.
    - **Faire preuve d’intégrité** : Vous respectez et promouvez les normes les plus strictes en matière de conduite éthique et professionnelle en relation avec les valeurs et le code de conduite de DRC, y compris la protection contre l’exploitation sexuelle, les abus et le harcèlement.
- Capacité à travailler dans un environnement multiculturel et cosmopolite
- Proactivité, avec une approche coopérative et collaborative
- D’excellentes capacités de communication (notamment l’attention et la patience) sont nécessaires
- De bonnes capacités organisationnelles sont requises
- Sens de l’éthique exemplaire
- Capacité à travailler en équipe et bon sens de l’humour

**6. Réglementations générales**

- Le/la Stagiaire doit suivre les instructions de DRC en matière de sécurité, de confidentialité et de directives éthiques, y compris le code de conduite et le cadre de responsabilité humanitaire
- Le/la Stagiaire ne doit exercer aucune autre activité rémunérée pendant la durée du contrat DRC sans autorisation préalable
- Le/la Stagiaire ne doit pas s'engager dans une activité qui pourrait nuire à DRC ou à la mise en œuvre de tout projet pendant la durée du contrat DRC
- Le/la Stagiaire ne doit pas accorder d'interviews aux médias ni publier de photos liées aux programmes de DRC ou partager d'autres documents sans en recevoir l’autorisation préalable
- Le/la Stagiaire doit restituer tout l'équipement prêté par DRC pour effectuer le travail après la fin de la période du contrat ou sur demande de DRC.

title: PIR Caseworker
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**   
The Caseworker provides trauma-informed, client-centered services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet immediate needs and support progress toward self-sufficiency. The role works closely with clients, internal teams, and external partners to develop and implement individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients to appropriate financial, medical, social, vocational, and community resources in alignment with program requirements, eligibility guidelines, and IRC standards.

**Major Responsibilities:**  
**Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:**

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure clients have access to housing, food, medical care, transportation, and community orientation.
- Conduct housing set-ups, airport pick-ups, home visits, grocery and public transportation orientation, and other field-based services to address immediate client needs.
- Purchase and transport program-related items; lift, move, and deliver materials necessary for service delivery.
- Conduct client intake assessments and develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with clients.
- Provide ongoing case management through direct services, referrals, advocacy, and coordination with internal and external service providers.
- Monitor client progress toward established goals, identify barriers, and adjust service plans as needed.
- Document all client interactions accurately and in compliance with program requirements; enter and maintain client data in required databases and tracking tools.
- Support Preferred Communities programming and intensive case management services, as assigned.
- Collaborate with colleagues across programs and grants to ensure clients access all eligible services.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community partners and service providers.
- Participate in program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds and compliance with grant requirements.
- Use a personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation to travel within the service delivery area as needed.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required.
- Experience providing casework, pre-arrival, or intensive case management services preferred.
- Demonstrated experience navigating program eligibility requirements and ensuring accurate service documentation.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Strong relationship-building, diplomacy, and networking skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Proven problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to use digital tools for data entry, research, and reporting.
- Ability to lift and carry items weighing 50+ pounds, including furniture and household goods.
- Ability to drive a large van or passenger vehicle, as required for program delivery.

**Compensation:** ($20.97). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Working Environment**

**This position operates in a hybrid environment that includes office-based work, remote work, and fieldwork within the service delivery area. Typically, the role is based in the office four days per week and remotely one day per week, with field responsibilities possible on all workdays. Schedule flexibility is required, including occasional evenings and weekends for activities such as airport pick-ups.**

At the IRC, we seek to build a welcoming, inclusive environment not only for our refugee clients, but for all of our employees. As an equal opportunity employer, we value the strength found in the diversity of voices, experiences, and backgrounds who join us in our work. Fostering an inclusive culture with equitable practices is everyone's responsibility, and we regularly offer trainings and opportunities to learn more and find ways to do better. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, socioeconomic status, or disability status. We are dedicated to ensuring that disabled individuals are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. In your application, please feel free to indicate your preferred pronouns.

We recognize that few applicants may "check all the boxes," but that each person has their own unique strengths that they would bring to the table. In our commitment to building a diverse and authentic work culture, we invite you to apply anyway. You belong here.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Housing & Integration Specialist
body:

A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:** The Housing & Integration Specialist supports the long-term housing stability, integration, and self-sufficiency of IRC clients by educating clients on their rights and responsibilities as tenants and assisting clients with applications, recertifications, and renewals for public and subsidized housing programs. This role focuses on empowering established clients to independently navigate and maintain their own housing over time.

**Major responsibilities include, but are not limited to:**

- Provide housing stability case management to IRC clients working toward long-term housing security and self-sufficiency, addressing needs that arise well beyond initial resettlement or arrival.
- Educate clients on tenant rights and responsibilities, lease renewals, move-in/move-out procedures, maintenance request processes, and change of address procedures, empowering clients with the practical knowledge to independently maintain stable housing and advocate for themselves as tenants.
- Providing financial education and coaching on budgeting for rent and utilities, housing costs and identifying housing that is sustainable based on household income.
- Assist clients with applications, recertifications, and renewals for public and subsidized housing programs (e.g., Housing Choice Voucher/Section 8, public housing authority programs, and other government rental assistance), including gathering documentation, completing forms, and following up with housing authorities and landlords to ensure continuity of housing.
- Identify clients at risk of eviction or housing loss and provide early intervention, connecting clients to emergency rental assistance and other resources, and advocating on clients' behalf with landlords and public housing authorities to prevent displacement.
- Maintain working relationships with public housing authorities, subsidized housing providers, and landlords to support clients' long-term housing stability. Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations to support clients' integration.
- Track program outputs and outcomes (e.g., households served through housing education, applications and renewals completed) and maintain accurate documentation and data entry in IRC's client database to satisfy funder and contract reporting requirements.
- May train and lead the activities of support staff, volunteers, and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

- Use personal, insured vehicle with valid driver’s license to travel to client homes, housing authorities, and community partners as needed throughout the service delivery area

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Superb organization, planning, and logistical skills.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Knowledge of, or ability to quickly learn, public and subsidized housing systems and processes (e.g., Housing Choice Voucher/Section 8) preferred.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time at partner sites—including apartment complexes and public/government service centers—within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

title: NVPPA Supervisor (Service Staff Supervisor)
body:
**IRC background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job overview**

*“This position has an end date of Month, Day, Year:”*

The National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement (NVPPA) is a nationwide, fully virtual program through which IRC will serve newly arrived refugees under a cooperative agreement with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). Participants receive career navigation, training, job placement support, and direct financial assistance to advance an individualized career goal.

The NVPPA Supervisor manages the day-to-day work of the program's direct service team across a fully virtual, national caseload. This role is responsible for caseload management, case file review, escalation and resolution of participant issues, and consistent quality across Professional Advancement Plans (PAPs) and uses of direct financial assistance.

**Major responsibilities**

**Supervision and caseload management**

- Manage day-to-day caseloads for direct service staff, including assigning and balancing participants across Career Navigators and routing participants on credentialing and recertification pathways to specialized navigators.
- Conduct regular case file review to confirm that participant records, including eligibility documentation, PAPs, and case notes, are complete, accurate, and timely.
- Resolve escalated participant issues in partnership with the Customer Service Representative, and determine when an issue requires the Deputy Director's involvement.
- Support onboarding and ongoing training of direct service staff.
- Translate program requirements into standard operating procedures and desk guides for the direct service team.

**Program quality and compliance**

- Review PAPs for soundness and confirm that career goals and proposed uses of funds meet ORR eligibility requirements before assistance is requested.
- Ensure required safeguards are applied to higher-risk uses of financial assistance, such as vehicle purchases.
- Work with the data team to ensure required data is recorded in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) and electronic case files are complete for ORR reporting.
- Monitor progress against program targets, identify barriers in the service model such as digital access, language access, or credential evaluation delays, and work with the Deputy Director on practical adjustments.

**Coordination**

- Coordinate handoffs among navigation, training, financial assistance, and job placement so that participants move smoothly through the program.
- Work with administrative and finance staff to ensure financial assistance requests are complete, documented, and aligned with each participant's PAP.
- Coordinate with other resettlement and employment programs, IRC offices, sister agencies, and local partners serving the same participants to support appropriate co-enrollment and avoid duplication of services.

**Job requirements**

- Undergraduate degree required, ideally in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field; comparable work and/or lived experience may be substituted.
- Minimum of 2 years of management or supervision experience required, including onboarding, coaching, and managing staff performance; experience with remote or distributed teams strongly preferred.
- Minimum of 2 years of relevant experience in human services, preferably in resettlement, workforce development, or employment services.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing high-volume caseloads in a compliance-heavy environment, including case file review and quality assurance.
- Demonstrated skills tracking and reporting information in a database; experience with ETO preferred.
- Familiarity with federally funded program compliance and eligibility documentation; experience with ORR-funded programming preferred.
- Experience developing standard operating procedures or workflow documentation, and familiarity with credential evaluation, professional licensing, or recertification pathways, preferred.
- Demonstrated commitment to client confidentiality and data protection, including oversight of how a remote team handles sensitive personal and immigration documents, required.
- Strong problem-solving, prioritization, and time management skills, and demonstrated success working in a multicultural environment.
- Commitment to anti-racism, ongoing learning, and equitable service to all eligible clients regardless of national origin, language, location, or resettlement agency, required.
- Lived experience as a refugee or immigrant preferred.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and remote collaboration tools required.
- Fluency in spoken and written English required; fluency in an additional language relevant to current refugee populations desired.

**Working environment**

- Fully remote, U.S.-based position requiring reliable high-speed internet and a private work space suitable for confidential client conversations.
- Scheduling flexibility is required to serve participants across U.S. time zones; occasional travel may be required.

**Compensation:** ($58,000 - $70,000 / Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403(b) retirement savings plan with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Deputy Director, NVPPA
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**SCOPE:**

*“This position has an end date of Month, Day, Year.”*

The Deputy Director, NVPPA provides leadership to the National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) funded program implemented in FY27. The Deputy Director leads the NVPPA team and ensures sound program implementation, compliance with ORR regulations, client success, and strong staff supervision and support.

NVPPA is a cooperative agreement carried out over a single 12-month period of performance, September 30, 2026 through September 29, 2027. The Deputy Director is accountable for delivering the program on time, within budget, and in compliance with the terms of the award.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Program Implementation and Deliverables***

- Lead program start-up so that intake, staffing, data tools, and referral protocols are in place as clients arrive, with interpretation and device support where access is a barrier.
- Set and enforce service standards across a high-volume, light-touch model, including a completed Professional Advancement Plan (PAP) and documented career navigation for every enrolled participant.
- Oversee delivery of training, job development, and placement support, and ensure related records are maintained.

***Grant Compliance and Award Management***

- Ensure the program is implemented in accordance with ORR policy, the terms of the cooperative agreement, applicable federal award regulations and cost principles, and IRC policies on data protection, client confidentiality, and safeguarding.
- In partnership with the Senior Director, serve as the program's primary point of contact with the ORR program officer and coordinate with ORR staff, partners, and technical assistance providers.
- Protect the integrity of program eligibility, ensuring eligibility rules are applied consistently and documentation is collected and retained for every enrolled participant.
- Own the internal control environment for direct financial assistance, including documentation before disbursement, alignment with the participant's approved PAP, vendor and training provider verification, and application of IRC Global Supply Chain protocols.
- Maintain audit-ready documentation and ensure required program and financial reports are accurate and submitted on schedule.
- Identify, escalate, and resolve compliance risks, including suspected fraud, working with IRC finance, compliance, and award management colleagues on corrective action.

***Budget and Financial Oversight***

- With the Finance Manager, manage the program budget, monitor spending, and ensure full and timely spend-down and closeout of the award.
- Where a shortfall is projected, provide revised projections and propose reallocation to additional eligible services or a budget revision, at ORR's direction.

***Data, Performance, and Quality Assurance***

- Ensure Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) is configured to program requirements and serves as the system of record, working with the data team on data quality, reporting, and staff training.
- Monitor performance against outcome targets and use data to identify barriers and adjust the service model.
- Establish and oversee a routine quality assurance cycle covering case files, PAPs, and assistance documentation, with findings tracked to resolution.

***Supervision and Staffing***

- Lead recruitment, hiring, and onboarding of a newly formed, fully remote team, and ensure all staff are trained on eligibility rules, eligible uses of funds, documentation standards, and the database.
- Directly supervise the NVPPA Supervisor and the Customer Service Representative, and manage performance, workload distribution, and professional development, and structure staffing so that direct service capacity can be adjusted as enrollment volume becomes known.

***Coordination and Representation***

- In close collaboration with the Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR), oversee guidance on appropriate co-enrollment with PIR and other ORR programs, such as Matching Grant, so that participants can meet initial self-sufficiency requirements while pursuing career goals.
- Establish referral and coordination protocols with sister resettlement agencies, IRC offices, and other service providers so that eligible clients can access the program regardless of which agency resettled them, and represent the program to IRC office leadership and external partners.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

**Position reports to:** Senior Director, Economic Empowerment

**Directly supervises:** NVPPA Supervisor; Customer Service Representative

**Indirect supervision:** Direct service team, through the NVPPA Supervisor

**Key relationships:** Internally, the NVPPA team, Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, IRC office leadership, and headquarters finance, compliance, and award management colleagues. Externally, ORR, PIR providers, sister resettlement agencies, training providers, and employers.

**Requirements:**

- University degree in Business, Public Administration, Social Work, Economics, Community Development, or a related field required; comparable work and/or lived experience may be substituted.
- Minimum of 10 years of experience with progressive responsibility in the design, development, and implementation of workforce, employment, or broader economic empowerment programming, including program monitoring and evaluation.
- Minimum of 5 years' experience managing staff, including remote or geographically distributed teams, with demonstrated ability to coach staff and manage performance directly and through supervisors.
- Demonstrated experience managing federally funded awards and their compliance and reporting requirements; ORR or other HHS award experience strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing client-level direct financial assistance or comparable payment processes, with a strong grasp of internal controls, required; experience with audits or funder monitoring preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to launch a program quickly and manage a budget of comparable scale through spend-down.
- Demonstrated understanding of refugee resettlement and employment services in the U.S. context; familiarity with credential evaluation and professional licensing pathways preferred.
- Excellent communication and organizational skills, including a track record of reporting difficult information to funders accurately and on time.
- Microsoft Office Suite required; ETO or comparable client database experience preferred.
- Commitment to anti-racism and ongoing learning, and English fluency, required.

**Working Environment**

Fully remote, U.S.-based position requiring reliable high-speed internet, a private work space suitable for confidential discussions, and scheduling flexibility across U.S. time zones; occasional travel may be required.

title: Liaison and Partnership officer
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified **Liaison and Partnership officer**.

## **About the job**

The Liaison and Partnership Officer supports DRC's access, operations, and partnerships across East (and South Libya when needed), under the line management of the Country Director and the technical supervision of the Partnerships Coordinator. This includes helping to build and maintain relationships with local authorities, civil society actors, humanitarian partners, and community leaders to support current and future programming.

The role requires a strong communicator who can navigate administrative systems and foster collaboration to support humanitarian goals, and who supports partner mapping, contract/sub-grant agreement (SGA) tracking, documentation and field follow-up in close coordination with the Partnerships Coordinator.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**1. Liaison and Representation**

- Serve as a focal point with local authorities including ministries and municipalities, and relevant entities in East and South Libya.
- Facilitate approvals, permits, and coordination required for operations, staff movement, and program implementation.
- Represent DRC in relevant coordination meetings and stakeholder forums to promote organizational interests and ensure alignment with local frameworks.
- Monitor and interpret local administrative and context developments that may impact operations.
- Jointly with DRC's partnership unit, liaise with sub-grant partners to ensure the process is clear and all documents are received and updated on the system.
- Demonstrate competencies in drafting official letters in both languages (Arabic and English).

**2. Operational and Program Support**

- Support field teams in obtaining timely approvals for program activities, site access, and logistical facilitation.
- Assist in resolving access challenges, bureaucratic bottlenecks, and operational impediments.
- Coordinate with logistics, security, and program teams to ensure smooth field operations and staff deployments.

**3. Engagement and Entry Point Analysis**

- Identify and assess opportunities for expanding or initiating programming in under-served or priority areas.
- Provide contextual analysis, local dynamics, and potential partners or entry points.
- Support needs assessments, field visits, and donor missions by organizing meetings and access arrangements with local actors.

**4. Partner Mapping, Contract and SGA Tracking**

- Support the mapping and regular updating of information on current and potential partner organizations (national/local NGOs and CSOs) operating in the area of coverage.
- Maintain and update the partnership database/tracker, ensuring partner profiles, capacity information and contact details are accurate and up to date.
- Ensure proper filing and archiving of partnership-related documents (MoUs, agreements, amendments, assessments, correspondence) in line with DRC's document management procedures.
- Maintain an up-to-date tracker of partner agreements/SGAs, including start and end dates, budget lines, deliverables and reporting deadlines.
- Follow up with partners and relevant internal teams on the status of agreement modifications, amendments, no-cost extensions and renewals, flagging any delays to the Partnerships Coordinator.
- Support the collection and compilation of documentation required for partner selection, due diligence and capacity assessment processes.

**5. Field Monitoring and Partner Follow-up**

- Support field visits to partner-implemented activities to follow up on progress against agreed targets and identify implementation challenges.
- Follow up on partners' compliance with agreement commitments and action points arising from monitoring visits, review meetings and audits.
- Document field visit findings and share reports/updates with the Country Director, relevant teams and the Partnerships Coordinator.

**6. Reporting and Documentation**

- Maintain records of key meetings, communications, and agreements with stakeholders.
- Support drafting of MoUs with partners, routing them for review and validation, and following up until finalization.
- Provide regular updates and analysis on access, coordination, and liaison matters to senior management.
- Contribute to reporting requirements for donors, clusters, and internal management as needed.
- Support the collection and follow-up of partner and community feedback related to partnership activities.
- Contribute inputs to internal partnership reports, trackers and dashboards for the Country Director and the Partnerships Coordinator.
- Flag any irregularities, compliance concerns or incidents identified during field visits or partner engagement to the line and technical manager.

**Note:** this job description must remain flexible, to respond to additional tasks or changes as identified by the line and/or technical manager.

## **About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have At least 2-3 years of relevant experience in humanitarian or development sectors, with exposure to liaison, coordination, external relations or partnership/grants support functions.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

**Required**

- Strong understanding of the context and humanitarian landscape in East and South Libya.
- Experience engaging with local authorities, community leaders, and civil society actors.
- Experience maintaining trackers/databases and working with Excel or similar tools for data and document tracking.
- Excellent communication, negotiation, cultural sensitivity, and interpersonal skills.
- Willingness to travel frequently and work in dynamic field environments.

**Desirable:**

- Experience working with both government and INGOs and/or UN agencies in a liaison role.
- Prior experience in access negotiation, humanitarian coordination, or partnership/grant support.
- Knowledge of humanitarian principles and operational standards; knowledge of donor compliance basics is an asset.

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

## **We offer**

- Contract length: Open Ended Contract
- Band: NMH2
- Designation of Duty Station: Benghazi Based (with regular travel to South and West of Libya plus Tunis when needed)
- Suggested Start date: 01 Nov 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-drc/vacancies). For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Us.

## **Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

**Closing date for applications: 27 October 2026**

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website [drc.ngo](https://drc.ngo/).

title: Chief of Party – ‘Catalyst Fund’ for Locally Led Humanitarian Response & Solutions
body:
**What we’re looking for:**

NRC is seeking an experienced **Chief of Party to lead the ‘Catalyst Fund’ for Locally Led Humanitarian Response & Solutions,** an ambitious new initiative transforming how humanitarian assistance is financed and delivered.

You will provide strategic leadership across countries, partners and workstreams, driving programme delivery, locally led partnerships, learning and humanitarian systems change. The Fund aims to strengthen local leadership in neglected displacement crises, initially in Africa, by combining rapid, flexible emergency response with locally led recovery, protection and sustainable pathways to solutions.

Beyond immediate impact, you will help shape a scalable model that strengthens local systems, promotes self-reliance, and influences wider humanitarian financing, policy and practice. The role is expected to begin with a six-month inception phase to establish the Fund’s operational model, partnerships, governance and learning systems, subject to final approval.

The ideal candidate must have a strong understanding of NRC’s internal systems, processes, and operational context.

**What you will do:**

**Strategy**

- Set the strategic direction of the Fund and ensure the effective functioning of its activation, assurance and accompaniment arrangements across all levels of governance and implementation.
- Working closely with the donor(s) and the Fund's governing bodies, develop and implement the Fund's multi-year strategy, including its results matrix, control measures and key performance indicators.
- Accountable for robust risk mapping of Fund activities and implementation of appropriate risk mitigation measures.
- Responsible for monitoring and reporting on progress against strategic objectives and KPIs to NRC leadership, donors, and the Fund's governing bodies.
- Co-responsible (with NRC Management and the donor) for identifying and developing additional funding opportunities and co-donor partnerships to grow the Fund.
- Responsible for the Fund's transition/continuity planning, including succession from the inception-phase support arrangements.

**Fund Management Team**

- Ensure the Fund has the appropriate capacity and expertise required for effective delivery, and lead/support the recruitment of dedicated Fund positions.
- Provide strategic and functional leadership to staff and functions supporting the Fund, through line management, and/or functional relationships, as appropriate to the final organisational set-up.
- Establish effective working relationships with relevant NRC functions and teams, including the Emergency Response, Operational Support and Governance, and Global Programme Sections, ensuring coherent and timely support to the Fund across programme, grants, partnerships, finance, MEAL, learning, communications, policy and advocacy, and other relevant functions.
- Maintain effective coordination with external or shared functions supporting the Fund, including the ICVA Local Coordination Adviser, as relevant.
- Budget holder for the Fund, managing its budget, assets and resources.
- Responsible for the review and submission of quality donor reports (programmatic and financial), evaluations, audits, and partner agreements/awards.
- Ensure Fund functions (grants, finance, MEAL, communications, learning) provide effective and timely support to country teams and partners.
- Ensure effective risk management, compliance and mitigation across the Fund Facility.
- Accountable for the Fund's legal and regulatory compliance, including donor agreements and relations with the donor.

**Governance**

- Convene and service the Fund's governing bodies (Steering Committee/Board), ensuring agreed courses of action are implemented, reported on and monitored.
- Responsible for presenting the Fund's roll-out and delivery to the Steering Committee/Board and participate in board discussions as the Fund's representative.

**Delivery**

- Review and sign off on Fund activations and awards, ensuring adherence to the Fund's proportionate due diligence and assurance model.
- Responsible for ensuring high-quality implementation of Fund-supported responses, and accountable for control measures for monitoring delivery, in coordination with the roving staff deployed and country-level structures.
- Ensure close coordination with Country Office management teams in the delivery of the response.
- Ensure that NRC policies on safeguarding, Safe and Inclusive Programming and community engagement, and equitable partnerships are upheld in the delivery of the response
- Ensure effective coordination with relevant NRC technical and thematic functions, drawing on their expertise and quality assurance to support delivery of the Fund's humanitarian response, localisation and solutions objectives.

**Representation, Learning and System Change**

- Represent the Fund with external stakeholders (the donor(s), other donors, UN agencies, INGOs, local actors, coordination bodies such as ICVA), with the aim of advancing the Fund's strategic objectives and catalysing buy-in from key stakeholders.
- Working with the Global Learning Advisor, drive the Fund's Learning Agenda, ensuring learning is captured and used to influence humanitarian policy, financing and coordination practice in support of locally led approaches.

Please download a more detailed[ **JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAJ-eEOULz8QL83qm6OBgM0AW43y3fnlgu7FkFqncRmupo?e=yLbQDq) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Minimum 7 years' experience in a senior management role (e.g. Country Director, Head of Programmes, Fund/Grant Facility Director) in humanitarian or development contexts.
- Strong understanding of NRC’s internal systems, processes and operational context.
- Proven experience managing humanitarian pooled funds, grant facilities, or complex multi-partner consortia.
- Experience in localisation and locally-led humanitarian response approaches.
- Effective communication, interpersonal, facilitation and diplomatic skills, including the professional credibility to provide coordination and guidance to a multi-disciplinary global team.
- Documented results related to the position's responsibilities.
- Fluency in English , both written and verbal, with strong writing and editing skills.
- Prior expertise in Sub-Saharan Africa displacement contexts is an advantage.
- French language skills are an advantage, given the Fund's initial geographic focus.
- Prior experience with fund facility programmes, or similarly structured multi-donor mechanisms, is an advantage.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: NRC’s HO in Oslo, Rep Offices in Berlin, Brussels and London, as well Employer of Records (EoR) listed countries. The position could also be hosted in Dakar and/or Nairobi on a Resident contract.
- Contract: 24 months
- Travel: Up to 40%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 11 on NRC’s Resident/National salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[*Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC*](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.
