title: Program Officer, Instructional Design & Multimedia
body:
*This position is contingent on receipt of grant funding.*

**Job Overview:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Program Officer for Instructional Design and Multimedia for Settle In, a program providing information and support for newcomers in multiple languages through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org.

This position designs and produces the learning experiences newcomers encounter across Settle In’s platforms. The role combines two areas of practice: instructional design—structuring multilingual, self-paced learning journeys that help newcomers build knowledge over time—and multimedia production—creating videos, graphics, and other assets that support the full range of Settle In content.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Design multilingual, self-paced learning journeys for newcomer audiences, including learning objectives, sequencing, knowledge checks, and reinforcement. Apply instructional design, adult learning principles, plain language standards, and translation-ready structure so that content is usable by newcomers with varying levels of literacy, digital literacy, and prior exposure to U.S. systems.
- In partnership with Switchboard’s Senior Program Officer, Instructional Design, establish instructional design standards for Settle In content and review materials developed by team members, subject matter experts, and contractors against those standards.
- Incorporating Switchboard’s established instructional design standards, recommend and implement improvements to Settle In’s instructional design practice, and update previously developed Settle In learning resources on an established review cycle.
- Create compelling, in-language multimedia content, including short-form video, infographics, motion graphics, and social media assets.
- Manage post-production of all finalized work, including Adobe Premiere project organization, color correction and grading, sound design, motion graphics, music editing, sequencing, export and compression for multiple platforms, and archiving.
- Coordinate with the multilingual Digital Community team on content creation, voiceover, subtitling, and translation review, and advise colleagues on audio and video recording tools and practices.
- Ensure final products are easy to understand, culturally appropriate, linguistically and factually accurate, accessible across web and mobile, and aligned with Settle In standards, newcomer needs, and funder requirements.
- Ensure all learning experiences and multimedia content meet accessibility standards (e.g., captions, alt text, screen-reader compatibility)
- Maintain visual and instructional consistency across Settle In's platforms (website, mobile app, social media)
- Coordinate and incorporate feedback across teams and projects and participate in user testing and other methods for optimization of content.
- Manage production timelines across concurrent projects and coordinate the work of external contractors, including videographers, designers, and translation vendors.
- Use platform data and user insights to set measurable goals for content and assess performance, and contribute to project reports, including monthly activity updates and performance monitoring reports.

*Other duties as assigned.*

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in instructional design, education, communications, or other relevant field (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum four years of professional experience combining instructional design and multimedia production, including creating multilingual digital content for diverse populations.
- Demonstrated experience designing self-paced learning for adult audiences, including experience with e-learning tools.
- Excellent command of video editing (Adobe Premiere) and graphic design software (Adobe InDesign, Canva), and knowledge of social media platforms, especially Facebook.
- Working knowledge of plain language principles and digital accessibility standards.
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting).
- Ability to manage complex projects on strict timelines, with excellent written and oral communication skills and strong attention to detail.
- Fluency in at least one of Settle In’s supported languages (Dari, Pashto, Spanish, and Haitian Creole) preferred.
- Previous experience working with refugee resettlement or other immigration pathways, and familiarity with ORR-funded programs.
- Ability to translate complex or technical information into clear, visual, and easy-to-understand learning content
- Experience engaging with external subject matter experts, consultants, or production vendors.

**Working Environment:**  This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $80,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Case Coordination Caseworker
body:
**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized. Follow up with any referrals made to other programs.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Position Reports to:**  Case Coordination Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

title: Various Countries - Head of Programmes
Program Lead, Ebola Response
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND:**

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you’re skilled and passionate, we would like to add your energy to ours.

Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies, leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action.

Active in public health, education in emergencies, cash and basic needs and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home. The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, ask ‘Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

**CONTEXT:**

The Ministry of Public Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared the country's 17th Ebola outbreak on May 15, 2026, following laboratory confirmation of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in Ituri Province. On May 17, 2026, WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), and it has since become the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in DRC and the fastest-expanding on record. The outbreak is unfolding in a highly complex humanitarian and security context marked by chronic insecurity, armed group activity, repeated population displacement, and high levels of cross-border movement, particularly with Uganda and South Sudan.

The IRC is supporting containment of the outbreak in Ituri and North Kivu. IRC's primary focus is to support existing primary health care (PHC) facilities to ensure safe continuity of services, strengthen infection prevention and control (IPC) practices and infrastructure, raise community awareness of behaviors that limit further spread, and reinforce the protective environment, including through MHPSS support.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

The position of **Program Lead, Ebola Response** (PL) is a member of the Ebola Response Senior Management Team and is integral to the successful implementation of IRC's programs in the affected provinces. Working under the direction of the Ebola Response Director, the PL will be responsible for overall leadership in the design, implementation, and management of the Ebola Response’s programs to address clients’ needs and priorities. She/he will be responsible for providing strategic direction of programs, conceptualizing and promoting innovations, and continuing to deepen the impact of IRC’s programs on the ground.

The PL assists the Ebola Response Director in the integrated planning and implementation of activities crucial to the success of local programs. This includes internal and external coordination and stakeholder engagement, including with donors, government and non-government partners, and IRC technical and regional support teams; overseeing multi-sector project design and implementation; managing sector teams to propose, coordinate, and deliver quality programs aligned with strategic priorities and beneficiary needs; and managing strategic funding opportunity tracking, partnering and pre-positioning decisions.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:**

***Program Strategy, Design and Fundraising***

- Lead the operationalization of IRC's current Ebola Response strategy and actively engage in strategic planning processes to shape the response's longer-term direction.
- Perform regular analysis of the outbreak and ensure IRC's strategy and operational presence is responsive to those needs and highly mobile program models.
- Work closely with Coordinators and HQ-based Emergency Unit and Technical Unit staff to ensure that project design reflects IRC's program quality standards and adheres to industry best practices.
- Lead efforts to achieve sustainable program growth, proactively identifying opportunities for new programming initiatives and placing particular emphasis on securing multi-year funding to sustain them.
- Provide leadership and strategic support to program and grants teams as they develop competitive, evidence-based, and cost-effective funding applications.
- Provide guidance, strategies, and tools to ensure that program choices are grounded in the findings of needs assessments (drawing on both primary and secondary data), rigorous analysis, meaningful input from affected communities, a thorough understanding of context, technical best practices, and operational viability.
- Formulate integrated program initiatives that allow technical sectors to complement one another, while promoting the mainstreaming of protection principles and gender-responsive approaches throughout programming.

***Program Management — Implementation, Monitoring and Evaluation***

- Provide overall leadership of IRC's Ebola Response program portfolio, ensuring strategic coherence, well-managed growth, and full compliance with IRC and donor regulations.
- Build the capacity of program team members, both individually and as a team.
- Work with Program Coordinators and the Operations team to develop and adapt detailed, realistic, and feasible implementation plans.
- Collaborate with the Senior Management Team to uphold management, compliance, and performance standards, and to maintain effective systems for budget, knowledge, and risk management.
- Support program staff in capturing, documenting, and disseminating lessons learned and best practices, feeding them into future project design.
- Work with program staff to develop robust monitoring and evaluation (M&E) plans, including methodologies and tools that strengthen data collection, analysis, and reporting quality.
- Review M&E and accountability data with program staff to identify and address gaps in operational performance.
- Champion IRC's "partner first" approach, building strategic, respectful, and empowering relationships with local organizations, and ensuring partners are actively engaged in decision-making, program design, and service delivery, positioning IRC as a partner of choice.
- Ensure partnership management is high-quality, accountable, and collaborative, including oversight of partner-led delivery, adaptive technical support, and consistent application of IRC's partnership framework and principles.

**Grants Management**

- Provide strategic leadership in developing and executing a comprehensive funding strategy: expanding and strengthening the donor base, driving excellence in grants management and compliance, strengthening program and grants information systems, and contributing to high-quality proposals and reporting.
- Oversee internal and external reporting in coordination with the Ebola Response Director across programs and finance, ensuring reports are well-written, timely, and meet donor, IRC, and partner requirements; conduct thorough review of all external reports compiled by the Grants Coordinator.
- Ensure Program Coordinators conduct routine monitoring visits to implementation sites to verify donor compliance and program quality.
- Work with Program Coordinators and the Grants and Finance teams to maintain sound budget management, expense control, and timely contractual documentation.
- Support the Grants Coordinator in leading Grant Opening, Monitoring and Closing Meetings with relevant departments, ensuring these occur on schedule, and that programming staff are well equipped to manage project budgets.
- Ensure Program Coordinators review Budget vs. Actual reports regularly, and provide the leadership needed for effective monthly grant review meetings.
- Mitigate financial risk by working with the Finance Department to ensure programming staff fully understand the financial and administrative processes involved across project budget cycles.
- Integrate partnership considerations into program design and Go/No-Go funding decisions, engaging partners proactively throughout program and project development.

**External Representation and Advocacy**

- Maintain a strong working knowledge of IRC's programming in the epicenter zones to represent IRC credibly in coordination forums and with implementing partners, authorities, and donors.
- Support the Ebola Response Director in cultivating donor relationships, including donor visits and the development of targeted advocacy.
- Build and sustain strong partnerships with implementing organizations through regular communication, cooperation, and joint decision-making where appropriate.
- Serve as the focal point for program-related communication between IRC's regional and global country programs.
- Identify and track funding opportunities in collaboration with technical teams.
- Guide programmatic input into advocacy and communications efforts, both in-country and globally.

**Staff Management and Development**

- Supervise Program Coordinators and program staff, setting clear expectations and objectives, providing proactive wellbeing support, and delivering timely, constructive feedback.
- Foster an inclusive team culture centered on achieving individual and team results, grounded in mutual respect, inclusion, trust, active listening, ownership, learning, accountability, and openness.
- Apply IRC's performance management system consistently, providing regular, thoughtful coaching, feedback, and professional development to direct reports, and ensuring they do the same for their own teams.
- Strengthen programming staff's project management skills and ensure new capabilities are applied on the job.
- Lead recruitment, hiring, and development of high-performing staff, preparing them for greater responsibility.
- Provide leadership to ensure successful rollout of and adherence to IRC's Global People and Culture Operating Policies and Procedures.
- Hold regular, high-quality 1:1s with each direct report (at least biweekly) balancing interpersonal connection with work priorities.
- Model and reinforce healthy work-life balance practices to support staff well-being.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

- **Position Reports to:** Ebola Response Director
- **Position directly supervises:** Ebola Response Program Coordinators (5)
- **Internal:** Ebola Response Senior Management Team members, Emergency Unit, Regional RPAS team, Finance department, Comms & ER, Regional and HQ Support Departments. Close collaboration with P&C on People matters.  
    The Program Lead will work in close coordination with the DRC Country Program leadership and technical teams to ensure alignment between Ebola response interventions and the broader country strategy, facilitate knowledge sharing, leverage operational and technical synergies, resource mobilization, and plan for the transition to the national program at the appropriate time, if the context permits
- **External:** Other humanitarian organizations operating in Ebola-impacted areas, authorities, UN agencies, community stakeholders and donors

**REQUIREMENTS**

- Minimum eight years of leadership experience in emergency, conflict and epidemic outbreak settings, including at least five years managing NGO programs. Prior experience in an Ebola outbreak would be an advantage.
- Demonstrated ability to think strategically and prioritize under pressure, with a track record of rapid, sound analysis of complex issues, strong decision-making, and translating strategic priorities into actionable operational plans.
- Proven experience managing protection, WASH, cash, and primary health programs, along with experience partnering with local organizations.
- Track record of delivering programs successfully in rapidly changing, complex security environments.
- Demonstrated experience with mobile program models and remote management.
- Demonstrated success developing winning proposals for public and private-sector donors.
- Proven leadership of multi-disciplinary, cross-cultural teams, with strong mentoring, coaching, motivational, and team-building skills.
- Demonstrated commitment to inclusion and fair treatment of staff, and ability to identify and address barriers to inclusion for marginalized groups in emergency response.
- Prior experience managing programs funded by government agencies, FCDO, ECHO, foundations, and private donors required; experience in competitive funding environments a plus.
- Demonstrated ability to deliver projects on time, within budget, and to expected results.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities effectively while maintaining high-quality outcomes.
- Experience working in DRC is an advantage.
- Fluency in English and French required.

*(Version Francaise)*

**CONTEXTE :**

Répondant aux pires crises humanitaires du monde, le personnel de l'International Rescue Committee est une force pour l'humanité et l'espoir. Si vous êtes compétent(e) et passionné(e), nous aimerions ajouter votre énergie à la nôtre.

Par le biais de son Unité d'urgence (EmU), l'IRC est l'une des plus grandes agences humanitaires au monde, menant des interventions d'urgence rapides qui apportent une assistance vitale, un rétablissement précoce et un soutien à la stabilisation aux personnes touchées par les conflits, les déplacements, les catastrophes naturelles et les urgences complexes dans de multiples contextes à travers le monde. Nous nous engageons à innover, à faire preuve d'agilité et à établir des partenariats solides pour mener une action humanitaire opportune et efficace.

Actifs dans les domaines de la santé publique, de l'éducation en situation d'urgence, de l'aide en espèces et des besoins de base, ainsi que de la protection et de la promotion des droits, nous accompagnons les personnes du danger vers un foyer. L'IRC reconnaît que les personnes touchées par une crise, et les acteurs qui leur sont le plus proches, sont les mieux placés, ont le droit, et devraient avoir le pouvoir et les ressources nécessaires pour répondre à la crise et impulser un changement durable. Nous nous engageons à augmenter la part du financement acheminée vers les acteurs locaux dans les situations d'urgence, à nous demander « Pourquoi ne pas établir un partenariat ? » chaque fois que nous planifions des programmes, et à nous associer en tant que partenaires égaux.

**CONTEXTE DE LA MISSION :**

Le ministère de la Santé publique de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) a déclaré la 17e épidémie d'Ebola du pays le 15 mai 2026, suite à la confirmation en laboratoire de la maladie à virus Bundibugyo (BVD) dans la province de l'Ituri. Le 17 mai 2026, l'OMS a déclaré l'épidémie Urgence de santé publique de portée internationale (USPPI), et celle-ci est depuis devenue la plus grande épidémie d'Ebola jamais signalée en RDC, ainsi que la plus rapide en termes d'expansion jamais enregistrée. L'épidémie se déroule dans un contexte humanitaire et sécuritaire très complexe, marqué par une insécurité chronique, l'activité de groupes armés, des déplacements répétés de population et des niveaux élevés de mouvements transfrontaliers, en particulier avec l'Ouganda et le Soudan du Sud.

L'IRC soutient l'effort de confinement de l'épidémie dans l'Ituri et le Nord-Kivu. L'objectif principal de l'IRC est de soutenir les structures de soins de santé primaires (SSP) existantes afin d'assurer la continuité sécurisée des services, de renforcer les pratiques et infrastructures de prévention et de contrôle des infections (PCI), de sensibiliser les communautés aux comportements qui limitent la propagation de la maladie, et de renforcer l'environnement protecteur, notamment par un soutien en santé mentale et soutien psychosocial (MHPSS).

**APERÇU DU POSTE :**

Le poste de Responsable de programme, Réponse Ebola (PL) est membre de l'Équipe de direction senior de la Réponse Ebola et joue un rôle essentiel dans la mise en œuvre réussie des programmes de l'IRC dans les provinces touchées. Sous la direction du/de la Directeur/Directrice de la Réponse Ebola, le/la PL sera responsable de la direction générale de la conception, de la mise en œuvre et de la gestion des programmes de la Réponse Ebola afin de répondre aux besoins et priorités des clients. Il/elle sera chargé(e) de fournir une orientation stratégique aux programmes, de conceptualiser et de promouvoir des innovations, et de continuer à approfondir l'impact des programmes de l'IRC sur le terrain.

Le/la PL assiste le/la Directeur/Directrice de la Réponse Ebola dans la planification intégrée et la mise en œuvre des activités essentielles au succès des programmes locaux. Cela comprend la coordination interne et externe et l'engagement des parties prenantes, y compris avec les donateurs, les partenaires gouvernementaux et non gouvernementaux, ainsi que les équipes techniques et régionales de soutien de l'IRC ; la supervision de la conception et de la mise en œuvre de projets multisectoriels ; la gestion des équipes sectorielles afin de proposer, coordonner et mettre en œuvre des programmes de qualité alignés sur les priorités stratégiques et les besoins des bénéficiaires ; et la gestion du suivi des opportunités de financement stratégiques, du partenariat et des décisions de pré-positionnement.

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS :**

**Stratégie de programme, conception et collecte de fonds**

- Diriger l'opérationnalisation de la stratégie actuelle de la Réponse Ebola de l'IRC et participer activement aux processus de planification stratégique afin de façonner l'orientation à long terme de la réponse.
- Effectuer une analyse régulière de l'épidémie et veiller à ce que la stratégie et la présence opérationnelle de l'IRC répondent à ces besoins ainsi qu'à des modèles de programmes hautement mobiles.
- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les Coordinateurs et le personnel de l'Unité d'urgence et de l'Unité technique basé au siège afin de garantir que la conception des projets reflète les normes de qualité des programmes de l'IRC et respecte les meilleures pratiques du secteur.
- Mener les efforts visant à assurer une croissance durable des programmes, en identifiant proactivement les opportunités de nouvelles initiatives de programmation, avec un accent particulier sur l'obtention de financements pluriannuels pour les pérenniser.
- Fournir un leadership et un soutien stratégique aux équipes de programme et de subventions dans l'élaboration de demandes de financement compétitives, fondées sur des données probantes et rentables.
- Fournir des orientations, des stratégies et des outils afin de garantir que les choix de programmation s'appuient sur les résultats des évaluations des besoins (à partir de données primaires et secondaires), une analyse rigoureuse, une contribution significative des communautés touchées, une compréhension approfondie du contexte, les meilleures pratiques techniques et la viabilité opérationnelle.
- Élaborer des initiatives de programmes intégrées permettant aux secteurs techniques de se compléter mutuellement, tout en favorisant l'intégration des principes de protection et des approches sensibles au genre dans l'ensemble de la programmation.

**Gestion des programmes — Mise en œuvre, suivi et évaluation**

- Assurer la direction générale du portefeuille de programmes de la Réponse Ebola de l'IRC, en garantissant la cohérence stratégique, une croissance bien gérée et la pleine conformité aux réglementations de l'IRC et des donateurs.
- Renforcer les capacités des membres de l'équipe de programme, à titre individuel et collectif.
- Travailler avec les Coordinateurs de programme et l'équipe des opérations pour élaborer et adapter des plans de mise en œuvre détaillés, réalistes et faisables.
- Collaborer avec l'Équipe de direction senior pour maintenir les normes de gestion, de conformité et de performance, ainsi que des systèmes efficaces de gestion budgétaire, des connaissances et des risques.
- Soutenir le personnel de programme dans la collecte, la documentation et la diffusion des enseignements tirés et des meilleures pratiques, en les intégrant dans la conception des futurs projets.
- Travailler avec le personnel de programme pour élaborer des plans de suivi et d'évaluation (S&E) solides, y compris des méthodologies et des outils renforçant la qualité de la collecte, de l'analyse et du reporting des données.
- Examiner les données de S&E et de redevabilité avec le personnel de programme afin d'identifier et de combler les lacunes en matière de performance opérationnelle.
- Défendre l'approche « partenaire d'abord » de l'IRC, en établissant des relations stratégiques, respectueuses et valorisantes avec les organisations locales, et en veillant à ce que les partenaires soient activement impliqués dans la prise de décision, la conception des programmes et la prestation de services, positionnant ainsi l'IRC comme un partenaire de choix.
- Veiller à ce que la gestion des partenariats soit de haute qualité, redevable et collaborative, y compris la supervision de la mise en œuvre menée par les partenaires, un soutien technique adaptatif et l'application cohérente du cadre et des principes de partenariat de l'IRC.

**Gestion des subventions**

- Fournir un leadership stratégique dans l'élaboration et l'exécution d'une stratégie de financement globale : élargir et renforcer la base de donateurs, viser l'excellence en matière de gestion et de conformité des subventions, renforcer les systèmes d'information sur les programmes et les subventions, et contribuer à des propositions et des rapports de haute qualité.
- Superviser le reporting interne et externe en coordination avec le/la Directeur/Directrice de la Réponse Ebola, à travers les programmes et les finances, en veillant à ce que les rapports soient bien rédigés, remis à temps et conformes aux exigences des donateurs, de l'IRC et des partenaires ; procéder à un examen approfondi de tous les rapports externes compilés par le/la Coordinateur/Coordinatrice des subventions.
- Veiller à ce que les Coordinateurs de programme effectuent des visites de suivi de routine sur les sites de mise en œuvre afin de vérifier la conformité aux exigences des donateurs et la qualité des programmes.
- Travailler avec les Coordinateurs de programme et les équipes des subventions et des finances afin de maintenir une gestion budgétaire saine, un contrôle des dépenses et une documentation contractuelle en temps voulu.
- Soutenir le/la Coordinateur/Coordinatrice des subventions dans la direction des réunions d'ouverture, de suivi et de clôture des subventions avec les départements concernés, en veillant à ce qu'elles se déroulent dans les délais prévus et que le personnel de programme soit bien préparé pour gérer les budgets de projet.
- Veiller à ce que les Coordinateurs de programme examinent régulièrement les rapports Budget vs Réel, et fournir le leadership nécessaire à des réunions mensuelles de suivi des subventions efficaces.
- Atténuer les risques financiers en travaillant avec le département des Finances afin de garantir que le personnel de programme comprenne pleinement les processus financiers et administratifs impliqués tout au long des cycles budgétaires de projet.
- Intégrer les considérations de partenariat dans la conception des programmes et les décisions de financement Go/No-Go, en engageant les partenaires de manière proactive tout au long du développement des programmes et des projets.

**Représentation externe et plaidoyer**

- Maintenir une solide connaissance des programmes de l'IRC dans les zones épicentres afin de représenter l'IRC de manière crédible dans les forums de coordination et auprès des partenaires de mise en œuvre, des autorités et des donateurs.
- Soutenir le/la Directeur/Directrice de la Réponse Ebola dans le développement des relations avec les donateurs, y compris les visites de donateurs et l'élaboration d'actions de plaidoyer ciblées.
- Établir et entretenir des partenariats solides avec les organisations de mise en œuvre grâce à une communication régulière, une coopération et une prise de décision conjointe le cas échéant.
- Servir de point focal pour la communication liée aux programmes entre les programmes régionaux et nationaux de l'IRC.
- Identifier et suivre les opportunités de financement en collaboration avec les équipes techniques.
- Orienter les contributions programmatiques aux efforts de plaidoyer et de communication, tant au niveau national qu'international.

**Gestion et développement du personnel**

- Superviser les Coordinateurs de programme et le personnel de programme, en fixant des attentes et des objectifs clairs, en apportant un soutien proactif au bien-être et en offrant un retour d'information constructif et opportun.
- Favoriser une culture d'équipe inclusive centrée sur l'atteinte de résultats individuels et collectifs, fondée sur le respect mutuel, l'inclusion, la confiance, l'écoute active, la responsabilisation, l'apprentissage, la redevabilité et l'ouverture.
- Appliquer le système de gestion de la performance de l'IRC de manière cohérente, en offrant un accompagnement, un retour d'information et un développement professionnel réguliers et réfléchis aux subordonnés directs, et en veillant à ce qu'ils fassent de même pour leurs propres équipes.
- Renforcer les compétences en gestion de projet du personnel de programme et veiller à ce que les nouvelles capacités soient appliquées sur le terrain.
- Diriger le recrutement, l'embauche et le développement de personnel performant, en le préparant à des responsabilités accrues.
- Assurer un leadership garantissant le déploiement réussi et le respect des politiques et procédures opérationnelles mondiales de l'IRC en matière de personnel et de culture.
- Tenir des entretiens individuels réguliers et de qualité avec chaque subordonné direct (au moins une fois toutes les deux semaines), en équilibrant le lien interpersonnel avec les priorités de travail.
- Modéliser et renforcer des pratiques saines d'équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie privée afin de soutenir le bien-être du personnel.

**RELATIONS DE TRAVAIL CLÉS**

- **Ce poste relève de :** Directeur/Directrice de la Réponse Ebola
- **Ce poste supervise directement :** les Coordinateurs de programme de la Réponse Ebola (5)
- **En interne :** les membres de l'Équipe de direction senior de la Réponse Ebola, l'Unité d'urgence, l'équipe régionale RPAS, le département des Finances, Communication & ER, les départements de soutien régionaux et du siège. Collaboration étroite avec le département P&C sur les questions de personnel.

Le/la Responsable de programme travaillera en coordination étroite avec la direction du Programme Pays RDC et les équipes techniques afin d'assurer l'alignement entre les interventions de la Réponse Ebola et la stratégie pays plus large, de faciliter le partage des connaissances, de tirer parti des synergies opérationnelles et techniques, de la mobilisation des ressources, et de planifier la transition vers le programme national au moment approprié, si le contexte le permet.

- **En externe :** autres organisations humanitaires opérant dans les zones touchées par Ebola, autorités, agences des Nations Unies, parties prenantes communautaires et donateurs.

**EXIGENCES**

- Minimum huit années d'expérience en leadership dans des contextes d'urgence, de conflit et d'épidémie, dont au moins cinq années à la gestion de programmes d'ONG. Une expérience antérieure dans une épidémie d'Ebola serait un atout.
- Capacité démontrée à penser de manière stratégique et à établir des priorités sous pression, avec un historique d'analyse rapide et rigoureuse de questions complexes, une solide prise de décision, et la capacité à traduire les priorités stratégiques en plans opérationnels concrets.
- Expérience avérée dans la gestion de programmes de protection, WASH, transferts monétaires et santé primaire, ainsi qu'une expérience de partenariat avec des organisations locales.
- Historique de mise en œuvre réussie de programmes dans des environnements sécuritaires complexes et en évolution rapide.
- Expérience démontrée avec des modèles de programmes mobiles et la gestion à distance.
- Succès démontré dans l'élaboration de propositions gagnantes pour des donateurs du secteur public et privé.
- Leadership avéré d'équipes pluridisciplinaires et interculturelles, avec de solides compétences en mentorat, coaching, motivation et renforcement d'équipe.
- Engagement démontré envers l'inclusion et le traitement équitable du personnel, et capacité à identifier et à surmonter les obstacles à l'inclusion des groupes marginalisés dans les interventions d'urgence.
- Expérience préalable requise dans la gestion de programmes financés par des agences gouvernementales, le FCDO, l'ECHO, des fondations et des donateurs privés ; une expérience dans des environnements de financement compétitifs est un atout.
- Capacité démontrée à mener des projets à terme, dans les délais, dans le respect du budget et conformément aux résultats attendus.
- Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités efficacement tout en maintenant des résultats de haute qualité.
- Une expérience de travail en RDC est un atout.
- La maîtrise du français et de l'anglais est requise.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Housing Specialist
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future

**Job Overview:** The UHP Housing Specialist secures and coordinates the furnishing of safe, sanitary, and affordable housing for newly arriving humanitarian parolees and refugees and provides related logistical support. This role will work with staff, clients, and community partners to stabilize humanitarian parolees/refugee and client households by connecting them with long-term resources for low-income and designated affordable housing opportunities. In coordination with the UHP Team, the UHP Housing Specialist will be responsible for locating housing for UHP clients and other vulnerable populations. The UHP Housing Specialist also participates, as required, in program planning and service developments through teams, committees and work groups. The UHP Housing Specialist operates under moderate supervision with latitude for the use of independent judgment and initiative.  
  
***This position has an end date of September, 30, 2027.***

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Identify and secure safe, sanitary, and affordable housing for newly arriving refugees in compliance with established program requirements.
- Conduct ongoing outreach to current and potential landlords and property managers, building strong working relationships with the goal of increasing access to housing for refugee families and to coordinate client home repair requests as needed. Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations to support a positive resettlement experience.
- Coordinate logistics of housing set-ups including ordering furniture and supplies and arranging delivery, arranging utility hook-ups, facilitating lease signings and renewals, arranging payments, and conducting home safety inspections.
- Implement a high-quality procurement protocol including researching potential new vendors, following appropriate financial and purchasing procedures, and maintaining required documentation.
- Deliver orientations to clients independently or in collaboration with housing caseworkers; may support other pre- and post-arrival activities such as airport pick-ups.
- Satisfy recordkeeping requirements.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of support staff, volunteers, and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree
- Minimum of 1 year of housing related professional experience required
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations preferred

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment
- Proven ability to contribute both independently and as a key team member
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively
- Superb organization, planning, and logistical skills
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product
- Ability to regularly lift ~50 lbs
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in Ukrainian and/or Russian language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is preferred.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work

**Compensation:** ($26/hr-$27/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

Cookies: [https://careers.rescue.org/us/en/cookiesettings](https://careers.rescue.org/us/en/cookiesettings)

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Country Director, Ethiopia
body:
**Job Title:** Country Director, Ethiopia

**Location:** Addis Ababa, Ethiopia (Only candidates who are eligible to work legally without work visa sponsorship in Ethiopia will be considered.)

**Contract Type:** Full-time (40 hours per week), 1-year fixed term contract with possibility of renewal based on funding and performance. This is a national position.

**Hiring Salary:** ETB 508,934 per month (before taxes)

**Target Start Date:** January 2027

**Application Closing Date:** October 20, 2026 23:59 EAT

This job advert is for an existing vacancy.

## **About Right To Play:**

For more than 25 years, Right To Play has been protecting, educating, and empowering millions of children each year to rise above adversity through the power of play.

We offer programs in 10 countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and North America, reaching millions of children each year in some of the most difficult places on earth, helping them to connect, learn and thrive. We do this by harnessing play, one of the most fundamental forces in a child's life, to equip children with the critical skills they need to dismantle barriers and embrace opportunities, in learning and in life.

This work is supported by our two global offices in Toronto, Canada and London, UK; and seven National Offices in North America and Europe.

Right To Play in Ethiopia is working with government, civil society organizations, communities, teachers and parents to increase access to quality education, enhance primary school children's learning and social emotional skills, promote children's access to inclusive, high quality, play-based Early Childhood Care and Education, provide play-based psychosocial support to improve the holistic well-being of children and young people and address the challenges that children face in host, internally displaced and refugee communities. Learn more about our programs in Ethiopia from [**our website**](https://righttoplay.com/en/countries/ethiopia/).

## **Benefits Highlights:**

- Connect and collaborate with a global team who are passionate about protecting, educating and empowering children and youth using the power of play!
- Culture premised on our **Culture Code (accept everyone, make things happen, display courage, demonstrate care, and be playful)**
- Paid leave (20 days annual leave and 3 personal days per year)
- Competitive benefits such as medical insurance for employee and eligible family members, life insurance for employee, transportation allowance, and communications allowance
- 10% temporary allowance for Ethiopia employees from October to December 2026 and the next salary review is in January 2027
- Learning opportunities and 5 learning and development (L&D) days per year
- Flexible work arrangements
- More information on what we offer is available on [**our website**](https://righttoplay.com/en/landing/why-join-us/).

## **Job Description:**

**Job Title:** Country Director (CD)

**Grade:** 11

**Reports to:** Vice President, Transformation and Impact

**Location:** Ethiopia

**Direct Reports:** Program Manager, Education Specialist, Finance Manager, People and Culture Specialist, MEL Specialist, Logistics Officer

**Department:** Global Program Unit

### **1.Purpose:**

Provides overall strategic and programmatic leadership including business development, fundraising, compliance and risk, financial and people management to ensure the success and growth of the country programme.

### **2.Accountability & Responsibilities:**

#### **Governance and representation (20%)**

- **Identifies and manages organisational risk**, including legal and governance matters, and acts as RTP’s legal representative in country.
- **Represents RTP at country level**, engaging government, donors, UN agencies, and NGO coordination platforms to build influence, credibility, and strategic partnerships.

#### **Fundraising and Communication (20%)**

- **Leads country-level fundraising and resource mobilisation**, driving proposal development, donor engagement, and diversified funding partnerships.
- **Leads in-country media and external engagement**, strengthening RTP’s profile and ensuring alignment with organisational values and objectives.

#### **Strategy development and implementation (15%)**

- **Sets and leads the strategic direction of the country programme**, ensuring alignment with RTP strategy, national priorities, and legal and regulatory requirements.

#### **Programmatic oversight, learning and innovation (15%)**

- **Oversees the country programme portfolio**, ensuring high-quality delivery, measurable impact for children and young people, and timely reporting to donors, government, and HQ.
- **Promotes collaboration and learning**, advising partners on play-based and sport-for-development approaches and embedding evidence-informed practice.
- **Champions innovation and continuous improvement**, driving excellence in programming and efficiency across internal systems and processes.

#### **Operational management (15%)**

- **Provides strategic oversight of finance and administration**, including budgeting, expenditure control, audits, grant compliance, and strong internal controls.
- **Holds overall accountability for safeguarding, safety, and security**, ensuring compliance with RTP policies and national legislation.

#### **Staff and workplace management (15%)**

- **Ensures effective people management**, including recruitment, performance management, learning and development, payroll, and the promotion of a safe and inclusive culture.
- **Leads, mentors, and develops a diverse country team**, fostering staff wellbeing, inclusion, and high performance.
- **Promote Safeguarding, foster a safe, respectful, and accountable work environment** by modelling appropriate conduct and addressing any behaviour that undermines a healthy workplace.

#### **Perform other duties as assigned**

### **3.Scope (geographical and/or functional), Impact and Autonomy:**

Oversees all aspects of the country office, providing guidance and support to the team, while serving on the Global Leadership Team to ensure quality program delivery, adherence to budgets, and contributing to global initiatives that enhance organizational systems and processes.

### **4.Leadership and Staff Management:**

Leads and develops the Country Management Team through coaching, mentoring, and capability-building while championing a safe, inclusive, and high-performing culture. Oversees People & Culture processes to ensure compliance, best practices, and effective performance management, upholding strong DEIA standards, staff safety, and well-being. Demonstrates integrity and resilience, proactively addressing and mitigating legal risks, including seeking legal advice when necessary.

### **5.Information Requirement for Decision-Making:**

Makes decisions based on a combination of internal and external information, often requiring an analytic approach to draw conclusions from incomplete information or non-conclusive information.

### **6.Innovation and Improvements**

Drives innovation and continuous improvement to deliver high-quality, impactful programs and more efficient internal systems and ways of working.

### **7. Relationships & Communications: Internal / External:**

Builds and sustains strategic relationships with key stakeholders, including donors, government officials, UN agencies, academia, media, NGOs, and local partners, while promoting RTP’s identity and relevance to the needs of vulnerable populations, in alignment with the localization strategy. Leads strategic donor, HQ visits, workshops, represents RTP in high-level meetings, conferences, and media to strengthen its profile.

### **8. Expertise (Certifications / Education, Professional Experience):**

- Extensive experience in leadership roles within a large or medium international development organization, including: strategic planning, leadership and people management, project management and planning, monitoring and evaluation and financial and risk management.
- Master’s degree in business administration, social sciences, development studies or related discipline.
- Experience working in or managing programmes in stable and fragile contexts.
- Proven success with mobilizing new sources of program funding.
- Understanding of laws, regulations and cultural dynamics local and international.
- Fluency in spoken and written Amharic and English Significant experience with a child-focused organization is desirable.

### **9.Core Competences:**

- **Collaboration:** Highly collaborative with strong interpersonal skills; excels at working in with a multicultural team and builds rapport and trust to develop strong external partnerships.
- **Growth Mindset:** Demonstrates commitment to own professional development and encourages their team to develop their potential, creates a learning culture through effective coaching and mentorship.
- **Communication:** Communicates complex operational, technical & strategic issues clearly & credibly to diverse audiences, leveraging strong networks to secure donor funding & influence stakeholders.
- **Resilience:** Strong organizational skills and the ability to work under pressure: multi-tasking, meeting deadlines, solving problems creatively and embracing challenges with resilience.
- **Professionalism:** Models professionalism and RTP’s values, promoting a safe, inclusive workplace and positive impact for children and youth.
- **Management and Interpersonal Skills**: Lead and mentor country team with influence, fostering trust, high performance, and shared ownership of outcome.

### **10.Additional Information:**

Expected to travel regularly domestically and occasionally internationally and work outside regular hours.

title: Client Voices Promoter
body:
**BACKGROUND:**

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 29 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC helps refugees resettle and become self-sufficient. Our programs are designed to ensure refugees thrive in America--whether ensuring children are enrolled in school, adults become self-reliant through employment or starting businesses, or families receive acute medical care they need to recover from trauma or illness. IRC Wichita has been assisting refuges since 2011. The Wichita office offers a range of services including trauma-informed family support, economic empowerment, education for youth and adults and immigration services. The IRC helps those in need to rebuild their lives and regain control of their future in their new home.

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

IRC believes that designing our strategies and programs based on clients’ particular needs and preferences is one of the most critical drivers of impact. We also believe that we have a role to play in working with clients so that they can engage as an equal, influential partner both with IRC and in the broader community through advocacy. The Client Voices Promoters will play a key role in supporting client engagement, and feedback initiatives at the local level. Promoters will work to bring together multi-ethnic, multi-racial and multi-sector constituencies to build the power of refugees and immigrants and the organizations that serve them to ensure their sustainability and improve people’s lives.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Partner with IRC program staff to execute client satisfaction and feedback initiatives, including surveys and focus group discussions.
- Collaborate with clients to ensure their feedback informs IRC program planning and service improvements.
- Identify and implement preferred client engagement and feedback methods tailored to community needs.
- Act as a liaison between IRC and local refugee communities, representing their concerns and suggestions to office leadership.
- Support client participation in discussions with external partners to amplify their influence on broader community strategies.
- Attend community events and workshops to maintain strong connections with refugee communities and identify areas for program enhancement.
- Organize and facilitate leadership and civic engagement training sessions to empower clients as advocates and community leaders.
- Coordinate community events and focus groups to encourage active client involvement in IRC decision-making processes.
- Ensure alignment with IRC’s client complaints and feedback policies, supporting consistent and ethical practices.
- Maintain accurate records of feedback and engagement initiatives to track progress and inform future strategies.
- Proactively engage with clients and raise their issues to IRC leadership to inform organizational priorities.
- Perform additional tasks as assigned to support IRC’s mission and client-centered programming.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

- Undergraduate degree preferred, in relevant field of study.
- Minimum 3 years of work experience.
- Demonstrated experience working with refugees, asylees, victims of human trafficking, and/or immigrant populations required.
- Community outreach experience preferred.
- Strong written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills: the ability to communicate effectively and build relationships with colleagues and partners in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment, and the ability to present to a varied public required.
- Solid organizational skills with the ability to juggle multiple tasks, set priorities, effectively manage time, and meet deadlines required.
- Fluency in English, both verbal and written, is required. Fluency in other languages and cultures of the local refugee population including Arabic, Swahili, French and Pashto/Dari is strongly preferred.
- A valid driver’s license, reliable vehicle with current insurance, and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area required.

**Working Environment:**

- Combination of working in a standard office environment and work in the community including meetings with community partners.
- Occasional weekend and/or evening work required.

 **Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Clinical Services Supervisor
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Seattle in 1976 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Seattle is committed to providing trauma-informed, inclusive and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Clinical Services Supervisor oversees and provides culturally, and linguistically appropriate mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) designed to improve the holistic well-being of human trafficking survivors. The position has four main functions: 1) Clinical services - conducting mental health intakes and assessments, developing individual service plans, and delivering evidence-based and evidence-informed interventions, 2) Clinical supervision - supervising non-licensed psychosocial support staff to ensure services are of quality, trauma informed, and culturally relevant, and 3) Care coordination - with internal and external providers to ensure holistic client support, and 4) Outreach and engagement - to build provider and community capacity to identify, respond to, and serve survivors of human trafficking. The Clinical Services Supervisor must be an independently licensed counselor/therapist in WA State. Strong candidates must have experience helping help high barriers clients navigate and access systems, and delivering culturally responsive, linguistically accessible services. This position reports to the MHPSS Program Manager with clinical supervision provided by IRC’s MHPSS Technical Advisor.

**Clinical Responsibilities:**

- Supervision
- Ensure clinical quality of programming
- Conduct intake and assessment and develop individual service plans
- Provide interventions and activities in-office, remotely, and in community settings
- Maintain a clinical case load (approx. 15-20 clients)
- Manage crisis (i.e., suicide assessments, safety planning, mandatory reporting, etc.)
- Care coordination including warm hand-offs as needed
- Support development and delivery of psychoeducation training to IRC staff and community partners to strengthen response and services for survivors of human trafficking.
- Supervise master’s level Practicum Interns

**Project Management Responsibilities:**

- Arrange for interpreters as needed to appropriately engage clients in services
- Ensure timely and accurate documentation, data entry, and reporting
- Monitor program activity and quality through oversight and support related to case and project documentation
- Evaluate effectiveness of program related to client progress and individual service plan objectives
- Communicate and coordinate regularly with all levels of program staff to ensure that services are being delivered effectively and in a timely manner
- Strengthen and maintain partnerships with community mental health agencies to expand client resources
- Deliver capacity-building initiatives to strengthen community response and services for human trafficking victims
- Other duties as assigned

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** MHPSS Program Manager

**Position Supervises:** WARN Mental Health MSW interns

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal*****:** *WARN Team, Family Wellness Team, Resettlement Team, Employment Team, Immigration Team, Youth Program Team, New Roots Team, Health Empowerment Team, Volunteer Coordinator, Finance Team, Operations Team, Development Team.*

***External*****:** *API Chaya, REST, KIND, Northwest Justice Project, Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, Seattle Police Department, US Attorney’s Office, Homeland Security Investigations, Washington Advisory Committee on Trafficking, City of Seattle Human Services Division, Washington State Office for Crime Victim Advocacy, Washington State Task Force Against Trafficking in Persons, and additional partners.*

**Job Requirements:**

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Holds a valid Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker (LICSW) in the state of Washington
- In accordance with state Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card
- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy

title: PIR Case Management Specialist
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Spokane in 2022 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Spokane is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Case Management Specialist provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. This position splits time between two programs: approximately 70% in ORR's Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR) and approximately 30% in the Home ARP program. The Case Management Specialist works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide case management services across two funding streams, dedicating approximately 70% of time to PIR clients and 30% to Home ARP clients, ensuring program requirements and documentation standards are met for each.
- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has essentials such as airport pick up upon arrival, initial and permanent housing, food, medical care, and access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Help clients find and apply for permanent housing and support them through the move-in process.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide services that are relevant to the client’s goals, including the distribution of direct financial assistance, applications for public benefits, referrals to medical and mental health services, and housing. Ensure active clients receive at least one meaningful interaction every 30 days, up to 90 days of service.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information into IRC’s case documentation database, ETO, and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.

title: Program Director for Europe
body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular Fixed Term (Fixed Term)

**Summary:**

Around the world, access to safe and decent shelter remains a fundamental human right—and across Europe, the challenge of building sustainable, equitable housing systems has never been more urgent. At Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI), we are driving transformative change to ensure everyone has a safe place to call home. To drive this regional impact, we are seeking a Program Director for Europe. In this regional leadership role, you will drive systemic impact across four core pillars: strategic portfolio leadership, technical and program quality, people and network leadership, and resource mobilization.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Portfolio Leadership**  
\* Develop, operationalize, and update the Europe Program Strategy in alignment with global and regional priorities.  
\* Translate strategy into clear multi-year objectives, delivery plans, resource allocations, and impact targets.  
\* Conduct regular portfolio reviews to scale, adapt, or exit programs and partnerships, ensuring focus on Habitat’s core comparative advantages.

**Technical Quality, Innovation & Systems Change**  
\* Position HFHI as a thought-and-practice leader across priority housing areas (e.g., energy efficiency, social rental, adaptive reuse, Roma housing, and displacement response).  
\* Lead and mentor a team of Subject Matter Experts (technical advisors) to drive evidence-based interventions.  
\* Oversee technical standards, quality assurance, and integrated approaches linking housing with climate, policy, finance, and social inclusion.

**Team Leadership & People Development**  
\* Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing, multidisciplinary Europe program team.  
\* Provide matrix leadership for cross-functional staff and foster a culture of trust, accountability, inclusion, and continuous learning.  
\* Manage capacity allocation across proposal design, technical support, and strategic initiatives.

**Network Collaboration & Governance**

\* Build strong strategic relationships with National Organizations (NOs), Global Foundations, and leadership boards.  
\* Represent and chair HFHI on National Organization Boards of Directors.  
\* Support country entities in strategic alignment, technical assistance, and capacity assessments while respecting local governance.

**Program Development & Resource Mobilization**  
\* Build a robust pipeline of scalable, fundable programs aligned with regional priorities.  
\* Lead the development of multi-country funding packages, concepts and consortium opportunities for EU institutions, development banks, foundations, and bilateral donors in close partnership with Resource Development.

**External Positioning & Influence**

\* Represent Habitat’s programmatic interests with EU institutions, governments, development banks, and housing networks.  
\* Translate program evidence into policy recommendations, annual engagement packages, and active coalition leadership.

**Area Leadership & Operations**  
\* Serve as an active member of the Europe & Middle East Area Leadership Team, contributing to organizational strategy, budgeting, and talent management.  
\* Act on behalf of the Senior Director for Programs when delegated.

**What do we require?**  
\* Master's degree in International Development, Public Administration, Social Sciences, or a related field.  
\* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in program management and leadership roles, with at least 5 years specifically focused on programs within Europe.  
\* Proven track record as a housing expert with deep operational and conceptual knowledge of regional housing challenges  
\* Familiarity with EU funding programs (such as LIFE and Horizon Europe)  
\* In-depth understanding of European development finance institutions  
\* Extensive experience in managing and leading multicultural teams.  
\* Fluency in English is required; proficiency in at least one other major European language (e.g., French, German, Spanish) is highly desirable.  
\* Strong understanding of the political, economic, and social landscape of Europe.  
\* Ability to travel extensively within Europe and to the global headquarters as required.  
\* Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.

\* Active support of HFHI Values:

\- Humility – We are part of something bigger than ourselves  
\- Courage – We do what’s right, even when it is difficult or unpopular  
\- Accountability – We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission

\* Safeguarding: HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work. Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct

**This position is based in Bratislava, Slovakia and requires 30% of travel.**

\#LI-DNI

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience.
